author: reek
body: The disk inventory. GopMedium answers one question in private -- which medium is mine -- and locks the answer into GopDisk's selection cells. This chapter answers the wider question out loud: what disks does this machine have at all? Every AHCI port, the NVMe namespace, the legacy IDE drive, the USB stick -- each named by its own IDENTIFY or INQUIRY data, sized in sectors, and probed for an EFI System Partition, its volume label, and our own CODEX.CDX. The demo this exists for: the boot stick lists every disk in the machine by name and points at itself.

author: reek
body: Enumeration rides the same seam the medium probe rides: steering the selection cells at a candidate makes the whole FAT stack above read from it. Unlike the probe, enumeration must leave no trace -- the cells are saved before the walk and restored after it, magic written last, so a locked boot medium stays locked and a cleared machine stays cleared no matter what the walk touched.

author: reek
body: The BPB carries the volume label at byte 43 on FAT16 and byte 71 on FAT32, eleven characters, space-padded.

author: reek
body: With the selection cells steered at a candidate, one mount answers whether it carries a FAT ESP at all, one boot-sector read yields the label, and one root-directory lookup answers for CODEX.CDX.

author: reek
body: Each candidate follows the same shape: prove the controller answers, steer the cells at it, probe its ESP, decode its identify data. The USB candidate exists only when usb-attach published a handle -- the connect fallback would reset the shared controller and kill the keyboard, the same rule GopMedium follows.

author: reek
body: Save the selection cells, walk every candidate, restore. The restore writes the magic LAST for the same reason med-set does: a partial write must never read as a selection.
